content: Melvin-Koushki says that in the view of medieval Muslim thinkers like Ibn ʿArabī and Ibn Turka after him, man is the singularity of creation, being and nonbeing, God's own portal to Himself; the purpose of creation is to produce the insān kāmil, the Perfect, Prophetic Man, who ascends (miʿrāj) to spirit and in descending returns to Nonbeing laden with revelation, so that the prophetic cycle leads to the end of history (maʿād), there to be transposed to a higher level and begin anew. The page cites no passage of Ibn Turka for this.
